documents.unit: Office of the President (AI at CMU, AI Advisory Board)
documents.title: AI at CMU: Policy and Guidance
documents.summary: Office of the President page setting out draft principles for CMU's AI use and campus expectations, centered on approved tools, no regulated data in generative AI, and compliance, and linking data policies 3-30, 3-31 and 3-42. On learning it only asks for clear syllabus and assignment guidance, so course-level AI rules are left to instructors.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule on student AI use in coursework; it says "Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions" and points to the teaching office, so the decision falls to instructors (delegates). Its binding rules concern university data, not learning.

units.why: The principle says "AI should enhance learning and prepare graduates for an AI-rich workplace", a stated rationale about careers, so it is P44 (professional skill) and informs rather than binds.
units.anchor: prepare graduates for an AI-rich workplace

units.why: "Provide equitable access to AI education and tools, with clear expectations for use" is an institutional principle on access, so P51; it is a "should"-style principle addressed to the university.
units.anchor: Provide equitable access to AI education and tools

units.why: "Institutional data stewardship and regulatory compliance are nonnegotiable" is a data-protection principle, so P50; it is stated as fact about priorities, hence informs.
units.anchor: Institutional data stewardship and regulatory compliance are nonnegotiable

units.why: "Be explicit about when and how AI is used; model proper attribution" asks for transparency and attribution, which matches P24 (disclose AI use) better than P47 because the principle is not limited to instructors.
units.anchor: Be explicit about when and how AI is used; model proper attribution

units.why: "Support with governance, staffing, and evaluation to ensure continuous improvement" commits to ongoing assessment and improvement, so P54 (revisit regularly) rather than P55, since no evidence-gathering on learning is named.
units.anchor: evaluation to ensure continuous improvement

units.why: "Draft policy principles emphasize academic integrity, data privacy and security, compliance..." sets the scope and principles of the university framework, so P56; it informs.
units.anchor: Draft policy principles emphasize academic integrity, data privacy and security

units.why: "Use institutionally approved tools when working with university data" tells people to prefer vetted tools for university data, so P50; imperative wording gives must.
units.anchor: Use institutionally approved tools when working with university data

units.why: "consumer tools are typically for public data only unless covered by an enterprise agreement" limits what data may go into consumer AI tools, so P50 (protect data, vetted tools).
units.anchor: consumer tools are typically for public data only

units.why: "Do not input regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, CUI, PCI) into generative AI tools" is a direct prohibition protecting confidential data, so P50 and must-not.
units.anchor: Do not input regulated data (e.g., HIPAA, CUI, PCI) into generative AI tools

units.why: "Follow all applicable laws/policies (e.g., accessibility, copyright, research integrity, data security)" is a general compliance principle for AI use; it fits the institution-wide framework P56 better than P52 since copyright is only one listed example.
units.anchor: Follow all applicable laws/policies (e.g., accessibility, copyright, research integrity, data security)

units.why: "Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions" tells instructors and units to state AI expectations, so P09 (statement in syllabus).
units.anchor: Provide clear guidance on acceptable use including syllabus statements and assignment directions

units.why: The Data Stewardship summary says the policy "prohibits entering institutional data into generative AI systems without proper prior written approval", a data-protection prohibition (P50).
units.anchor: prohibits entering institutional data into generative AI systems without proper prior written approval

units.why: "Users may not upload CMU data to generative AI systems without prior written approval" forbids uploading university data to AI, so P50 rather than P49, which concerns course materials.
units.anchor: Users may not upload CMU data to generative AI systems without prior written approval

units.why: The Information Security Policy "reinforces requirements for protecting institutional data when using AI technologies", a data-protection statement informing readers of the rule (P50).
units.anchor: reinforces requirements for protecting institutional data when using AI technologies

units.why: "Community members are expected to follow these policies whenever using AI tools in teaching, learning, research, or administrative work" sets the scope of the framework for all AI use, so P56.
units.anchor: Community members are expected to follow these policies whenever using AI tools

units.why: "CMU continues to evaluate policies and practices to address emerging AI-related opportunities and risks" says policy will keep being reviewed, so P54.
units.anchor: CMU continues to evaluate policies and practices

documents.unit: Office of Curriculum and Instructional Support
documents.title: Planning for AI in Teaching and Learning
documents.summary: Teaching-support guidance that helps faculty decide a course-level and assignment-level AI approach, using three starting-point approaches (limited, guided, integrated). It advises starting from learning goals, stating expectations in the syllabus and in class, and attending to privacy and access, but sets no mandatory student rule.
documents.stance_why: The page says "There is no single approach to AI that will work for every course" and offers three approaches (limited, guided, integrated) for faculty to choose from, so it hands the decision to instructors and lists tiers; stance is delegates.

units.why: "There is no single approach to AI that will work for every course, discipline, or assignment" leaves the choice to each course, so P04; it is a statement of fact (informs).
units.anchor: no single approach to AI that will work for every course

units.why: "The goal is not to adopt AI simply because it is available or to avoid it entirely" is a principle that takes a neutral middle line and asks for intentional decisions; P04 (instructor decides) fits better than P02 or P03.
units.anchor: not to adopt AI simply because it is available or to avoid it entirely

units.why: "The role of AI should be determined by the purpose of the learning experience, not simply by the tool's capabilities" tells instructors to set the rule per learning experience (P04).
units.anchor: determined by the purpose of the learning experience, not simply by the tool's capabilities

units.why: "Your approach to AI may vary across courses—and even across assignments within the same course" says the rule is set per course or assignment, so P04 (not P11, which is about non-carryover to students).
units.anchor: Your approach to AI may vary across courses

units.why: The page offers three named approaches ("AI use is limited", "AI use is guided", "AI use is integrated") as "a useful starting point", i.e. named tiers of use (P05).
units.anchor: The following three approaches can provide a useful starting point

units.why: "The use of AI may be restricted when students need to develop or demonstrate essential skills independently" limits AI to protect skill building, so P41 (practice builds skill) rather than P01 since it is conditional.
units.anchor: AI may be restricted when students need to develop or demonstrate essential skills

units.why: Under the "limited" approach, listed cases include "Completing exams, quizzes, or other assessments of independent learning", i.e. AI restricted on assessments (P22); modality may because the page is advisory.
units.anchor: Completing exams, quizzes, or other assessments of independent learning

units.why: "Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work" describes limiting AI early and allowing it later, so P08 (stage permission as skills develop).
units.anchor: Developing skills they will need before using AI responsibly in more advanced work

units.why: "Limiting AI does not mean ignoring its existence. Students still benefit from understanding why its use is restricted" asks instructors to explain the reason for limits; fits P41 (rationale for limits).
units.anchor: Students still benefit from understanding why its use is restricted

units.why: In the guided approach "faculty clearly identify which uses are permitted, which are not, and how students should document their use of AI", an instruction to state expectations in the course, so P09; documentation is mentioned but not the main point.
units.anchor: faculty clearly identify which uses are permitted, which are not
units.frag_start: In a guided approach, faculty clearly

units.why: Students "might be permitted to use AI to: Brainstorm possible topics" is an example permitted use, so P15 (brainstorming).
units.anchor: Brainstorm possible topics

units.why: "Generate practice questions" is a listed permitted use of AI in the guided approach, so P14 (practice and study aids).
units.anchor: Generate practice questions

units.why: "Create an initial outline" is a listed permitted use; an outline is writing support, so P18 (prose) rather than P15.
units.anchor: Create an initial outline

units.why: "Receive suggestions for revising grammar or organization" is a listed permitted use for writing, so P18.
units.anchor: Receive suggestions for revising grammar or organization

units.why: "Explore alternative explanations of a difficult concept" is a listed permitted use where AI acts as a tutor, so P12.
units.anchor: Explore alternative explanations of a difficult concept

units.why: In the integrated approach "AI is not completing students' learning. It becomes material for analysis, decision-making, and reflection", a redesign of work around AI (P35) rather than P02.
units.anchor: AI is not completing students' learning. It becomes material for analysis, decision-making, and reflection

units.why: Students "might be asked to: Critique an AI-generated response" and "Identify inaccuracies, bias, or missing perspectives" teaches critical checking of AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: Identify inaccuracies, bias, or missing perspectives

units.why: "Explain which parts of the output they accepted, changed, or rejected" is a reflection on AI use that students submit, so P26.
units.anchor: Explain which parts of the output they accepted, changed, or rejected

units.why: Question 1 asks faculty to "Identify the knowledge and skills that students must practice without AI assistance", tying limits to skill building (P41).
units.anchor: Identify the knowledge and skills that students must practice without AI assistance

units.why: "AI use should extend or support the learning process rather than replace it" says AI should not replace student thinking, so P32.
units.anchor: AI use should extend or support the learning process rather than replace it

units.why: "If AI can complete the most important thinking required by the assignment, the expectations or design may need to be reconsidered" advises redesigning assignments, so P35.
units.anchor: the expectations or design may need to be reconsidered

units.why: "Clearly communicate whether AI is permitted, limited, required, or prohibited for each major assignment" asks for explicit expectations per assignment (P09).
units.anchor: Clearly communicate whether AI is permitted, limited, required, or prohibited for each major assignment

units.why: "Consider whether students will need to create an account, pay for access, enter personal information" raises access and privacy burdens, so P51 (equitable access).
units.anchor: Consider whether students will need to create an account, pay for access

units.why: "When AI use is required, provide an appropriate alternative for students who cannot use the selected tool or prefer not to" is an equity alternative (P51).
units.anchor: provide an appropriate alternative for students who cannot use the selected tool

units.why: "A syllabus statement can explain your overall approach to AI" lists contents (permitted, limited, prohibited), so it recommends a syllabus statement: P09.
units.anchor: A syllabus statement can explain your overall approach to AI

units.why: The syllabus should state "Student responsibilities for accuracy and source verification", so P31 (verify AI output).
units.anchor: Student responsibilities for accuracy and source verification

units.why: The syllabus should state "Expectations for acknowledging AI use", so P24 (acknowledge AI use).
units.anchor: Expectations for acknowledging AI use

units.why: The syllabus should say "How students should ask questions when expectations are unclear", so P10.
units.anchor: How students should ask questions when expectations are unclear

units.why: "Whatever language you choose, discuss it with students rather than relying on the written statement alone" advises talking through the policy; fits P09 (communicating expectations).
units.anchor: discuss it with students rather than relying on the written statement alone

units.why: "Consider discussing AI expectations early in the semester and again when introducing major assignments" is advice on communicating expectations (P09).
units.anchor: Consider discussing AI expectations early in the semester and again when introducing major assignments

units.why: Discussion topic "How to ask for clarification before using a tool" encourages students to ask before using AI, so P10.
units.anchor: How to ask for clarification before using a tool

units.why: "Faculty expertise remains essential for evaluating accuracy, appropriateness, and alignment with learning goals" is a reminder about instructor judgment; closest fit is P59 (instructor role in teaching work), though it is a statement of principle.
units.anchor: Faculty expertise remains essential for evaluating accuracy, appropriateness, and alignment with learning goals

units.why: "Students should not enter private, protected, or personally identifiable information into public AI tools" protects personal data (P50).
units.anchor: Students should not enter private, protected, or personally identifiable information into public AI tools

units.why: "AI-generated information may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or supported by fabricated sources" warns that output may be wrong, so P31.
units.anchor: AI-generated information may be inaccurate, biased, incomplete, or supported by fabricated sources

units.why: "Students remain responsible for the work they submit" is an ownership statement (P29).
units.anchor: Students remain responsible for the work they submit

units.why: "Expectations should be communicated at both the course and assignment levels" asks for communication at two levels (P09).
units.anchor: Expectations should be communicated at both the course and assignment levels

units.why: "CMU faculty can receive support with: Developing course or assignment-level AI expectations" offers consultations to faculty, so P63.
units.anchor: CMU faculty can receive support with

documents.unit: Office of Curriculum and Instructional Support
documents.title: Sample Statements for Teaching Syllabi
documents.summary: A library of syllabus template statements from the teaching office. The AI-relevant parts are a modified academic integrity statement and an optional AI statement, both prohibiting submission of AI output as one's own and leaving any permitted use and citation method to the instructor.
documents.stance_why: The page is a menu of template language, and the optional statement says "If the use of AI tools and platforms is appropriate within the context of a course, guidance ... will be provided by your instructor", so the permission decision is delegated while the template itself bans passing off AI output as one's own.

units.why: The modified integrity statement says dishonesty includes "submitting artificial intelligence (AI)-generated products as your own original work" and calls it prohibited; students may not submit AI output as their own, so P19.
units.anchor: submitting artificial intelligence (AI)-generated products as your own original work, is prohibited

units.why: The same sentence places AI-generated work under "Academic dishonesty, which includes cheating, plagiarism..." so unauthorized AI is classed as misconduct (P36); the P19 unit covers the rule itself.
units.anchor: Academic dishonesty, which includes cheating, plagiarism, and other forms of dishonest or unethical behavior

units.why: "This modified statement includes suggested language regarding AI-related content" tells instructors a template with AI wording exists for syllabi, so P09.
units.anchor: This modified statement includes suggested language regarding AI-related content

units.why: "Faculty should adapt these examples to match their course outcomes, disciplinary expectations, and planned learning activities" leaves the final wording to instructors, so P04.
units.anchor: Faculty should adapt these examples to match their course outcomes

units.why: The optional statement defines its scope as "Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Google AI, Boost.ai, Jasper, etc.)", a definition of AI tools (P61).
units.anchor: Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) tools and platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Google AI, Boost.ai, Jasper, etc.)

units.why: "products generated by AI tools and platforms as your own original work is prohibited" bans submitting AI output as one's own, so P19.
units.anchor: products generated by AI tools and platforms as your own original work is prohibited

units.why: "a violation of CMU's Academic Integrity policy" classifies such submission as misconduct handled under the integrity policy, so P36.
units.anchor: a violation of CMU's Academic Integrity policy

units.why: "If the use of AI tools and platforms is appropriate within the context of a course" leaves permission to each course, so P04 (instructor decides).
units.anchor: If the use of AI tools and platforms is appropriate within the context

units.why: Guidance and "appropriate methods of citation for direct quotations, ideas, diagrams, code, or paraphrased text generated through AI will be provided by your instructor", so students cite AI as the instructor directs (P24).
units.anchor: appropriate methods of citation for direct quotations, ideas, diagrams, code

notes: Coder A. Only the AI-relevant parts of the sample-statements page were coded. Topic codes were chosen by meaning because AGENT_BRIEF.md was not consulted.
